summary: Intermittent 429s during scheduled batch pulls — suspected rate-smoothing/refill misalignment
description:
Issue summary: Customer SparkMaps reports repeated 429 responses during their scheduled batch pulls that run every 5 minutes. The failures are concentrated in a 10–20 second window at the start of each scheduled job.

Impact: Intermittent 429s affecting approximately 15% of batched API calls for the customer's dedicated tenant for ~2 hours after deployment changes. No data loss reported but job retries cause elongated job completion and downstream latency spikes.

Environment: prod - us-east (dedicated pool, tenant ID redacted in ticket). Using redwood-1-small for embeddings/generation and open-7b-v2 for reranking.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Schedule 50 parallel workers to start at the same cron time (every 5 minutes).
2) Each worker opens a short-lived streaming session and issues a 1–3 token warmup call followed by concurrent batch calls.
3) Observe 429s during the first 10–20s of the window; error rate drops to normal after the first refill interval.

Expected behavior: Smooth token accounting across rolling windows; scheduled bursts should be absorbed by burst credits or smoothed by refill window.

Actual behavior: Short window of concentrated 429s on tenant APIs at the scheduled job start. Rate headers from requests show near-zero refill immediately after midnight-aligned refill boundary; tenant token bucket appears depleted earlier than expected.

Logs & evidence: Support attached request traces and rate headers from one affected window (see attachments). Kernel-level rate-limiter logs show a refill event at 00:00:00 that leaves a residual mismatch between per-route accounting and tenant aggregation. Latency traces show retries concentrated on the first 18s.

Customer ask: Guidance on configuration to avoid synchronized refill spikes; temporary mitigation to reduce immediate job failures while we investigate server-side accounting behavior.
comments: 2026-03-05 09:12 - Maya Singh (Support): Opened ticket after receiving customer logs. Requested timeline of their cron and number of parallel workers.

2026-03-05 09:45 - Liam Carter (SRE): Confirmed we see a refill boundary aligned to round minutes. Hypothesis: small smoothing window + synchronized worker start causes transient double-counting between route and tenant layers.

2026-03-05 10:10 - SparkMaps (customer): Confirmed they start 50 workers exactly at the cron time and can't easily jitter due to pipeline orchestration. Asked for quick mitigation to drop error rate below 1%.

2026-03-05 11:00 - Liam Carter (SRE): Applied temporary server-side smoothing increase for tenant (lengthened refill smoothing window by 2s) — initial metrics show 429 spike reduced to ~3%. Monitoring continuing.
2026-03-06 08:30 - Maya Singh (Support): Noted customer still seeing rare spikes when pipeline rebalances; scheduled call for 2026-03-06 to align on long-term fix and runbook updates.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Synchronized worker starts coincide with refill boundary and small smoothing window leads to refill accounting drift between per-route and tenant aggregators.
Hypothesis B: Short-lived streaming sessions are creating ephemeral tokens that are not reclaimed immediately on disconnect, causing momentary bucket exhaustion during bursts.

What we observed: Rate-limiter server logs show per-route counters decrementing before tenant-level aggregates reflect refill. Reproducible in a controlled test when starting 40+ parallel short sessions at the same timestamp.

Metrics: Token consumption spike measured at ~1200 tokens/sec for tenant during first 12s of window; burst credit was exhausted and tenant-level throttle applied. After smoothing window increase, peak dropped to ~950 tokens/sec and 429s reduced substantially.
Related config: Customer is on Dedicated pool with default smoothing window=500ms and burst-credit=2000. Their worker orchestration doesn't jitter start times.

Action taken: Short-term smoothing window increased to 2.5s for customer's tenant and server-side backfill to align route->tenant accounting. Added increased logging around disconnect reclaim events for streaming sessions.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: Extended refill smoothing window from 500ms -> 2.5s for tenant during high-frequency scheduled jobs. This reduced immediate 429 spike from ~15% -> ~3%.
Workaround for customer: Stagger job start times by 1–3s per worker if possible; add small jitter to cron and slow-start workers in orchestrator (example script provided in comment).

Long-term plan: Engineering to roll a patch that aligns per-route accounting with tenant-level refill events (PR referenced), and add a configurable per-tenant scheduled-job guardrail to auto-apply jitter or local burst credits for scheduled cron bursts.

Follow-ups: Update Runbook 'Rate Smoothing Runbook' with this pattern, add automated detection to Console that surfaces synchronized start spikes for dedicated tenants, and schedule postmortem with SRE + Platform on 2026-03-10.
Status: In Progress — monitoring metrics steady; awaiting engineering rollout of alignment patch (linked PR).
